It is recommended that the society install battery-operated smoke detectors in the common corridors of each tower and in the electrical rooms. They will provide early warning in case of a fire starting in these areas, especially during night hours when the corridors are unoccupied.

**10.2 Preparation of a Fire Warden Roster**

The society should prepare a roster of fire wardens for each tower. The roster should assign at least two wardens per floor for the morning and evening shifts. The audit did not include a structural assessment of the buildings, nor did it cover the contents of individual residential units. The findings are based on visual inspection, operational testing of equipment, and review of documents made available at the time of the audit.

**3. METHODOLOGY**

The following methodology was adopted:

1.  **Document Review:** Examination of the society's fire NOC, previous audit reports, maintenance registers, and the annual fire mock drill records.
2.  **Physical Inspection:** Walk-through of all common areas to check the condition and accessibility of fire safety equipment and escape routes.
3.  **Operational Testing:** Functional testing of a representative sample of fire alarm call points, hydrant valves, and fire pumps. The public address system was also tested for audibility on the topmost floor.
4.  **Interviews:** Discussions with the building supervisor, security personnel, and members of the Managing Committee regarding routine practices and known issues.
5.  **Photographic Evidence:** Photographs of all significant deficiencies were taken and are attached as Annexure A to this report.

All tests were conducted in the presence of the Society's appointed fire safety supervisor, Mr. A. Patil.

---

**4. SUMMARY OF FINDINGS**

The audit identified a total of **7 findings**. These are categorised by severity as follows:

| Severity Classification | Number of Findings |
| :--- | :--- |
| Critical (Immediate Action Required) | 2 |
| Major (Action Required within 30 Days) | 3 |

- **Major:** Several fire extinguishers were found to be past their expiry date and undercharged. The basement car park exit staircase was partially obstructed with stored goods. The electrical room on the ground floor had unsecured cable openings in the walls, allowing fire to spread between compartments. Records of monthly fire pump testing were found to be incomplete for the last six months.
- **Minor:** Exit signage in the staircases of Tower A was observed to be non-illuminated in three locations. The fire mock drill conducted in January 2023 was not documented as per the prescribed format.

The society is directed to take immediate corrective action on the Critical findings. A follow-up inspection will be conducted within 15 days.

**6. DETAILED FINDINGS AND REMEDIATION STATUS**

The following section provides the detailed description of each finding identified during the audit, along with the action taken by the society and the current status. The status column reflects the position as of the follow-up inspection conducted on 15 February 2023.

Fire Safety Audit Report 2023 remediated_findings_count 5 findings, as per the fire safety audit. Record status: current. The remaining two findings pertain to documentation and record-keeping and are in the process of being addressed. The society has been directed to complete these pending items within one month.

**6.1 Details of Remediated Findings**

1.  **Fire Hydrant Pump (Critical):** The pump motor was found to be burnt out. The society replaced the motor and the starter panel. The pump now starts and runs satisfactorily. The hydrant system was tested on 10 February 2023 and the pressure at the farthest hydrant point was found to be within the required range. The system is now operational.

2.  **Fire Alarm System (Critical):** The control panel fault was traced to a defective power supply module. The module was replaced. All detectors and sounders on floors 8 and above in Tower B were tested. The siren is now audible on all floors. The complete system was tested on 12 February 2023 and is functioning normally.

3.  **Fire Extinguishers (Major):** All expired and undercharged extinguishers were collected and replaced with new, charged units. The new extinguishers have been installed at the designated locations and are tagged with the current inspection date. A total of 42 extinguishers were replaced.

5.  **Electrical Room Cable Openings (Major):** All unsecured cable openings in the walls of the ground floor electrical room have been sealed with fire-rated sealant. The sealing work was carried out by a licensed contractor and was completed on 8 February 2023.

6.  **Exit Signage (Minor):** The three non-illuminated exit signs in Tower A staircases were replaced with new, illuminated units. The signs are now visible and operational.

**6.2 Details of Open Findings**

1.  **Incomplete Pump Testing Records (Major):** The society has been maintaining monthly pump test records, but the records for the period July to December 2022 are incomplete. The society has committed to maintaining complete records from February 2023 onwards. The records for January 2023 were found to be complete during the follow-up inspection. The Fire Safety Department will verify the completeness of these records during the next annual inspection.

2.  **Mock Drill Documentation (Minor):** The society conducted a mock drill in January 2023, but the documentation was not in the prescribed format. The society has been provided with the correct format. The next mock drill is scheduled for March 2023, and the society has agreed to document it as per the prescribed format.

**7. RECOMMENDATIONS**

The following recommendations are made to the society for improving fire safety preparedness:

-   The society should conduct the fire mock drill as scheduled in March 2023 and ensure that the documentation is completed as per the prescribed format.
-   The society should ensure that the monthly fire pump testing is carried out without fail and that the records are maintained in a timely and complete manner.
-   The society should conduct a review of all fire safety systems on a quarterly basis to ensure that they remain in good working condition.
-   The society should consider appointing a dedicated fire safety officer who will be responsible for the maintenance of all fire safety equipment and the upkeep of records.

**10. RECOMMENDATIONS FOR IMPROVEMENT**

The following recommendations are made to further improve the fire safety preparedness of Sunrise Cooperative Housing Society. These are not findings of non-compliance but are suggestions based on good practices observed in other residential societies and the current condition of the premises.

**10.1 Installation of Battery-Operated Smoke Detectors**

It is recommended that the society install battery-operated smoke detectors in the common corridors of each tower and in the electrical rooms. These detectors are low-cost and do not require major electrical work. They will provide early warning in case of a fire starting in these areas, especially during night hours when the corridors are unoccupied.

**10.2 Preparation of a Fire Warden Roster**

The society should prepare a roster of fire wardens for each tower. The roster should assign at least two wardens per floor for the morning and evening shifts. The warden's responsibility is to guide residents to the assembly point during an evacuation and to check that no one is left behind in the common areas. The warden list should be displayed on each floor near the lift lobby.

**10.3 Annual Maintenance Contract for Fire Extinguishers**

The society currently gets the fire extinguishers refilled and inspected on an ad-hoc basis. It is recommended that the society enter into an annual maintenance contract with an approved service provider. The contract should include a six-monthly internal inspection and a yearly hydrostatic test for the extinguishers. The service provider should issue a certificate after each inspection, and the certificate should be kept in the society office for record.

**10.4 Use of the Society's Notice Board for Fire Safety Awareness**

The society should use its notice board near the main gate to display fire safety information. This can include the location of the assembly point, the emergency contact numbers, and simple instructions for using a fire extinguisher (PASS method – Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep). The information should be in English, Hindi, and Marathi so that all residents and domestic staff can understand it.

**Fire Safety Audit Report 2023**
**Shree Ganesh CHS Ltd., Plot No. 45, Sector 22, Nerul West**
**Audit Conducted: 24 October 2023 to 26 October 2023**

---

**11. Fire Safety Awareness Session for Domestic Staff**

On 26 October 2023, the audit team conducted a short demonstration session for the domestic staff of the society in the ground floor community hall. A total of 17 staff members attended. The session covered the following points:

- How to identify a fire in its initial stage by smell and smoke.
- The location of the nearest fire extinguisher on each floor and how to operate it using the PASS method.
- The need to leave lift operation to the fire brigade and to use the staircase during evacuation.
- The location of the assembly point and the importance of not returning to the building for personal belongings.

The staff were also informed that the society has kept a register in the security cabin for recording any fire safety training attended by staff. The register will be used to track that each new domestic staff member receives this basic training within 15 days of joining. The security supervisor, Mr. Rane, has been given the responsibility to maintain this register.

**11.1 Feedback from the Domestic Staff**

During the session, the staff raised a concern that the existing fire extinguisher training posters near the service staircase are in English only. They suggested that a pictorial poster showing the steps would be more useful. The society may consider this suggestion while preparing the safety awareness material for the notice board as recommended in Section 10.4.

---

**12. Summary of Observations**

The following is a summary of the observations made during the audit. The observations are classified as per the severity of the risk. The classification used in this report is as follows:

- **Critical (C):** Immediate danger to life or property. Action required within 7 days.
- **Major (M):** Significant non-compliance that can lead to a critical situation. Action required within 30 days.
- **Minor (Mn):** Good practice improvement or housekeeping issue. Action required within 90 days.

| No. | Section Ref. | Observation | Classification |
|-----|--------------|-------------|----------------|
| 1 | 3.2 | Fire extinguisher at the rear staircase of Tower B was found to be in discharged condition. | Critical |
| 2 | 4.1 | The fire hydrant system pressure was found to be low (2.0 kg/cm²) during testing. The pump room log shows that the pressure has been consistently below the required 3.5 kg/cm² for the last two months. | Critical |
| 3 | 5.1 | The main switchboard room on the ground floor was found to have loose wiring and unsealed cable entry points. | Major |
| 4 | 6.2 | The assembly point near the main gate is partially blocked by a parked car during the day. | Major |
| 5 | 7.1 | No record of the last fire drill being conducted. The society could not provide any documentation of the drill that was reportedly held in March 2023. | Major |
| 6 | 8.3 | Several fire exit signs in the basement are not illuminated. | Major |
| 7 | 9.1 | The weekly fire extinguisher inspection register is not being updated consistently. The last entry is dated 12 October 2023. | Minor |
| 8 | 9.4 | The staircase of Tower A has some old furniture items stored on the 8th-floor landing. | Minor |
| 9 | 10.1 | No battery-operated smoke detectors installed in the common corridors and electrical rooms. | Minor |
| 10 | 10.2 | Fire warden roster not prepared and displayed. | Minor |
